What This Page Is

This page catalogs every person named in the book, identifies who they are using public records, and documents the relationships and behaviors Banks described in his own words.

Fair use notice: All excerpts are used for criticism, commentary, and public-interest reporting under 17 U.S.C. § 107. See the companion analysis for the full fair use framework.

  3. Met Banks for lunch at Brandy’s restaurant on Telegraph in Pontiac through mutual friend Roeiah
  4. Discussed her morning docket with civilians at the restaurant: Banks writes that “Judge Langford Morris was describing her morning docket to Roeiah and the other young lady and the various cases that she had heard.” A sitting judge describing active cases she heard that morning to non-lawyers at a restaurant.
  5. Invited Banks back to her courtroom and paraded him to staff
  6. Attended MSU Law BLSA events at Banks’s invitation
  7. Treated Banks to dinner when he “graduated from law school” — along with “several other judges”
  8. Banks volunteered on her Michigan Supreme Court campaign
  9. Wrote the foreword to a book branded “Brian Banks, J.D.” — endorsing the credential fraud of the felon she sentenced

What Banks confesses she did:

  • Discussed active cases with civilians in a restaurant (Canon 2, Rule 2.10 — Judicial Statements on Pending Cases)
  • Developed a personal ex parte relationship with a former defendant
  • Used a former felon defendant for campaign labor
  • Endorsed credential fraud in a published book foreword

Banks writes: “Retired Judge Vonda Evans and I became friends almost sixteen years ago. Vonda and I met through a mutual attorney friend one summer while hanging out in downtown Detroit.”

What Banks confesses she did:

  • Provided campaign strategy advice for a nine-time convicted felon running for office
  • Arrived at Banks’s grandfather’s hospital with Judge Cylenthia Miller — demonstrating personal, not professional, relationship
  • Was present the night before the grandfather’s death alongside Gay-Dagnogo

And: “my big sister, Cylenthia, and I survived.”

All excerpts are used under the fair use doctrine, 17 U.S.C. § 107, for purposes of criticism, commentary, and public interest reporting.

Four-factor fair use analysis:

  1. Purpose: Non-commercial criticism, commentary, and public-interest journalism. This site has no advertisements, no donations, no monetization. The purpose is to protect 362 children attending schools operated by the book’s author.
  2. Nature of the work: A published autobiography — the lowest tier of copyright protection. Self-published, commercially available, and branded with credentials the author does not hold.
  3. Amount used: Selected excerpts only, each accompanied by original commentary and cross-referenced against independently verifiable public records. No chapter is reproduced in full.
  4. Market effect: None. Amazon ranked this book #2,637,193 in Kindle Store (per M.L. Elrick, Detroit Free Press, 2022). This commentary does not substitute for the original work.

The book’s own copyright page states: “a reviewer may quote brief passages in a review.” This is a review.

The book is also a party admission under Michigan Rule of Evidence 801(d)(2)(A) — Banks’s own published statement, offered against him as a named party in pending litigation (Mok v. Banks et al., Case No. 2026-4349-CZ, Ingham County Circuit Court). Every word is admissible. No foundation required beyond authentication. The ISBN authenticates it.

Banks has no copyright claim that survives fair use. An attempt to suppress this analysis would constitute a SLAPP action against protected criticism of a public figure (former State Representative) regarding matters of profound public concern (credential fraud affecting public schools).

The Credential Fraud Begins on the Cover

Banks’s biography page — the final section of the book — reads:

“Honorable Brian R. Banks, M.Ed., J.D.”

Three false credential claims in six words:

  1. “Honorable” is a title reserved for judges and elected officials. Banks resigned from the legislature in 2017 after his ninth conviction. He is not a sitting official.
  2. “J.D.” implies a licensed legal practitioner. Banks has never been admitted to any bar.
  3. The biography states he aspired to “become a prominent attorney and, then, sit on the bench as an officer of the court” — admitting the exact goal he has been fraudulently representing as achieved.

The biography further claims:

“He has earned a Juris Doctor with a Concentration in Criminal Law from Michigan State University College of Law”

True. He earned the degree. He was never licensed to practice.

“Mr. Banks is a highly sought-after consultant, educator, organizer, assistant, community, political, legal mind and now, an author.”

“Legal mind.” Not “attorney.” Not “licensed.” The phrasing is a carefully constructed near-claim — close enough that readers assume licensure, vague enough to defend as technically truthful. This is how credential fraud works when the person committing it went to law school.

The book refers to this prosecution six times. Banks frames it as political persecution. The public record shows a guilty plea.

“I had been working part-time at a funeral home for number of years”

Major C. Clora Jr. is the current PCA Board Assistant Treasurer and owner of Clora Funeral Home in Detroit. Clora attended Wayne State’s Mortuary Science program. Banks was at Wayne State and considered mortuary science as his major before switching to Criminal Justice.

The Apology That Never Comes

Across 184 pages and approximately 55,000 words, Brian Banks does not:

The word “lie” appears once — as a confession:

Why This Book Is Evidence

Michigan Rule of Evidence 801(d)(2)(A) — Party Admissions

Banks is a named party in Mok v. Banks et al., Case No. 2026-4349-CZ. Every word in this published book is admissible against him as a party-opponent statement. It is not hearsay. No foundation is required beyond authentication — and authentication is trivial for a published book with an ISBN.

The Book Is Not a Memoir. It Is a Confession.

Brian Banks wrote a book under the name “Brian Banks, J.D.” and published it while unlicensed. He listed himself as “Honorable” on the biography page. He named every major node in his institutional network in the acknowledgments. He confessed to a decade of criminal activity in his own words. He documented improper judicial relationships with three sitting judges. He described his economic unit with a three-time convicted felon as “a permanent fixture in our family.”

Then he called it a “#1 Bestseller” when Amazon ranked it 2.6 millionth.

Everything about this man is a fraud — including his book sales.

The Right Turn Project’s Treasurer (Carlton Ross) is connected to the vendor (Ross Catering) that received campaign payments. There is no indication this occurred.

3. Dissolved Entity Operations

The Right Turn Project was dissolved December 1, 2021. Under MCL 450.2831, dissolved corporations may only wind up affairs and liquidate assets — they may not conduct new business. Any transactions after dissolution raise compliance questions.

4. Convicted Felon as Nonprofit Officer

Joseph Holland (MDOC #443789, convicted cocaine dealer) served as President and Registered Agent of the Right Turn Project and currently serves as Treasurer and Secretary of Purpose Foundation. While Michigan law does not categorically prohibit convicted felons from serving as nonprofit officers, organizations receiving public funds or serving vulnerable populations (children) face additional scrutiny.

5. Unauthorized Practice of Law Concerns

Banks operated Serenity Guardianship Services Inc (LARA 802290962) as a for-profit corporation from 2019-2023, serving as sole officer. Guardianship work in Michigan involves petitioning courts, managing wards’ legal rights, and filing accountings — activities that constitute the practice of law under MCL 450.681. Banks was never admitted to any bar.

6. Entity Formation Patterns

The dissolve-and-reform pattern (Custom Promotions Inc dissolved February 2022 → Custom Promotions LLC filed May 2022) may be used to shed liabilities while maintaining brand continuity. The three-name dark money vehicle (Save Detroit Jobs → Impact Detroit → Detroit Leaders) allows the same entity to operate under different public identities for different audiences.

How to Verify

Every entity on this page can be verified at Michigan LARA Business Entity Search:

  1. Go to the search page
  2. Enter the Entity ID number in the search field
  3. Select “Entity ID” as the search type
  4. All officer names, addresses, filing dates, and assumed names are publicly displayed

This is not a dossier. It is an index of public records with analysis of what those records reveal when connected.

  • Institutional Capture Graph — Full network visualization with 98 nodes and 160 edges.

entry.title: The Credential Gap — MacDowell Staff Qualification Audit
entry.content:
The Michigan Online Educator Certification System (MOECS) is the public database where anyone can verify whether a Michigan educator holds a valid teaching certificate, administrator certification, or permit — and which grade levels and subjects each endorsement covers. 📄 Documented

On September 26, 2026, every name listed on MacDowell Preparatory Academy’s public staff roster (macdowellprep.com/about/) was searched in MOECS. The audit found that only 2 of 14 instructional staff members are properly credentialed and correctly placed for their teaching assignment. 📄 Documented

Staff Roster Results 📄 Documented

Administration — 4 positions ($603,000/year combined)

RoleMOECS StatusIndicator
Superintendent/CAO (Brian Banks)Convicted felon (ICHAT SID 2029469K). School Administrator certificate only — no teaching credential.❌
Dean of Scholars + Culture (Cameron Coleman)Standard teaching certificate expired 6/30/2026. No administrator certification for Dean role.⏳
Dean of Academics (Kellie M Stevens)Standard teaching certificate (K-5/K-8 elementary). No administrator certification for Dean role.⚠️
Dean of Operations + 8th Grade Teacher (Chalcee Norwood)Not found in MOECS public search — 91 “Norwood” results searched, no match for “Chalcee”. Zero credentials discoverable.❌

Instructional Staff

RoleMOECS StatusIndicator
Kindergarten (Rachel Webb)Holds Secondary English/Journalism 6-12 certification. Zero elementary endorsement. Teaching kindergarten with a high school certificate.⚠️
Kindergarten (Lakeisha Bates)“No matches found” in MOECS. Zero credentials.❌
3rd Grade (Alana Hubbell)Daily Substitute Permit issued through Escuela Avancemos — a different school.🔶
5th Grade (Ashlie Spencer)Daily Substitute Permit issued through Chandler Park Academy — a different school.🔶
8th Grade Teacher (Volanda Frazier)Full-Year Basic Substitute permit only — no standard teaching certificate. Assigned as full-time Teacher of Record.⚠️
2 instructional staffProperly credentialed and correctly placed for their assignment.✅
2 staffExpired or pending credentials.⏳

Legend: ✅ Valid · ⚠️ Wrong endorsement/placement · ❌ No credentials · 🔶 Substitute permit from other school · ⏳ Expired

Source: MOECS public credential search, September 26, 2026. Staff titles from macdowellprep.com/about/.

The Rachel Webb Finding 📄 Documented

A kindergarten teacher holds a Secondary English/Journalism certification endorsed for grades 6–12.

Elementary education in Michigan requires a specific endorsement in early childhood or elementary education. A 6–12 secondary certification does not qualify an educator for K–5 instruction under Michigan law. MOECS shows Rachel Webb’s only endorsements are English 6–12 and Journalism 6–12 — neither covers kindergarten.

The Substitute Permit Problem 📄 Documented

Two MacDowell instructional staff hold Daily Substitute Permits issued through different schools:

StaffAssignmentPermit Issued Through
Alana Hubbell3rd GradeEscuela Avancemos — Detroit
Ashlie Spencer5th GradeChandler Park Academy — Harper Woods

Daily Substitute Permits are tied to the issuing school and are intended for temporary fill-in duty, not permanent full-time instructional positions. Using substitute permits from other schools to staff ongoing teaching roles is a credential compliance issue under Michigan law.

Volanda Frazier holds a Full-Year Basic Substitute permit as the full-time 8th grade Teacher of Record — a separate but related compliance problem.

The Law — MCL 388.1763 📄 Documented

Michigan Compiled Laws require charter school teachers to hold valid credentials:

“A teacher employed by or assigned to a public school academy shall hold a valid Michigan teaching certificate or a permit issued by the superintendent of public instruction.”

Penalty provisions when violations are found:

StatuteRequirement
MCL 388.1763(1)A district shall not employ an individual who is not appropriately placed under a valid certificate.
MCL 388.1763(2)50% state aid deduction for salary paid during the violation period.
MCL 388.1763(6)If a school official is notified by MDE and knowingly continues to employ an uncredentialed individual → misdemeanor, $1,500 fine per incident.

When MDE identifies credential violations, the statute requires enforcement — state aid deductions for uncredentialed employment and, where officials continue employment after notification, referral for criminal prosecution.

What MDE Did 📄 Documented

MDE was notified of credential problems at MacDowell. Over a four-year period, the Office of Educator Excellence investigated only one name — Brian Banks — in February 2022. The investigation was closed within approximately two hours after OEE Analyst Katie Schmiedeknecht communicated that “there will be no need for an investigation.”

MDE never checked the rest of the staff roster — despite MOECS and the Educator Registry (REP) being MDE’s own systems, searchable by any analyst in minutes.

Schmiedeknecht presents at state conferences on the same credential compliance rules she is charged with enforcing — including slides stating that “Any teacher who is not appropriately placed may be subject to a salary deduction based on MCL 388.1763.” Her office failed to enforce those rules at MacDowell while advising the school through the compliance loophole that avoided penalties for Banks.

Source: MDE FOIA response (September 25, 2026); MOECS public search (September 26, 2026).

Verify It Yourself

Anyone can reproduce this audit in minutes:

  1. Go to MOECS public search: mdoe.state.mi.us/MOECS/PublicCredentialSearch.aspx
  2. Enter the teacher’s last name
  3. Check: Is the certificate valid? Is it endorsed for the grades and subjects being taught?
  4. Compare results to the school’s actual staff roster at macdowellprep.com/about/

Discrepancies between MOECS endorsements and classroom assignments are visible immediately in the public record.

The Cost 📄 Documented

MacDowell Preparatory Academy serves 362 students. Four administrators draw $603,000/year in combined compensation:

MetricMacDowellContext
Admin cost per student$1,665/studentMichigan state average: approximately $850/student
Instructional spending32% of budgetMichigan target: 55–65%

Administration at nearly twice the state average per student diverts public funding away from instruction — in a school where MOECS already shows that most instructional staff lack proper credentials for their assignments.

This analysis is based entirely on MOECS public search results and Michigan Department of Education records. Every credential status can be independently verified using the steps above.
